parole.significato: A Balinese shaman or traditional healer.
A traditional Balinese and Javanese sweet made with rice flour or sago noodles and coconut milk
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Balinese ᬘᬾᬦ᭄ᬤᭀᬮ᭄ (céndol, “rice or sago syrup”) or Javanese ꦕꦺꦤ꧀ꦝꦺꦴꦭ꧀ (cèndhol, “protuberant”), from Old Javanese ceṇḍol. First attested in the Tantri Demung found at Sidemen Karangasem district in Bali, 1728 AD, as ᬘᬾᬦ᭄ᬤᭀᬮ᭄ (céndol).

The palmyra or leaves of this tree as used for palm-leaf manuscripts in parts of Indonesia and Malaysia.
parole.testo: From Balinese lontar, Indonesian lontar, from Old Javanese rontal.

parole.significato: In Bali, a Hindu priest or priestess.
parole.testo: From Balinese pedanda, padanda, ultimately from Sanskrit.

parole.significato: A suicidal march towards an enemy as carried out by the aristocracy or ruling class of a Balinese kingdom.
In Bali and other parts of Indonesia, a palace, or other residence of a member of the royal family or ruling class.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Balinese ᬧᬸᬭᬷ (puri), from Old Javanese purī (“palace, royal residence”), from Sanskrit पुरी (purī), पुर् (pur, “stronghold, fortress”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(t)pĺ̥H (“city, fortress, stronghold”). Compare to English polis (“a Greek city-state”). Doublet of Puri and pol

parole.significato: A communal organization for the irrigation of paddy fields on Bali.
